issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently uses two different method names for the same concept: the UML and many tasks reference messageOnFeed() as the abstract feeding method, while other parts of the text (e.g., the feedAllAnimals description and animal-specific return-value instructions) refer to getFeedingSound(). This naming inconsistency can confuse students about which method to implement and call (messageOnFeed() vs getFeedingSound()). The solution and intended design use messageOnFeed(), so the occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem text are inconsistent with the UML and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent throughout the problem statement. Replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed() (or vice versa) so they match the UML and the solution. Also update the textual descriptions that state feedAllAnimals() should call getFeedingSound() to state it should call messageOnFeed().

issues.description: The problem statement uses two different method names for the same concept of an animal's feeding sound: the UML and many task descriptions refer to messageOnFeed(), while several places in the textual tasks refer to getFeedingSound(). The solution code implements messageOnFeed(), and the template/starter files expect students to implement methods according to the UML. This inconsistent naming in the problem description (messageOnFeed vs getFeedingSound) can confuse students about which method to implement and which method the Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSong() should call.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() (as shown in the UML and solution) throughout the problem statement and in descriptions of Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSong(). Replace occurrences of getFeedingSound() in problem_statement.md with messageOnFeed(), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the template/solution to getFeedingSound()—but ensure all descriptions, templates, and solutions use the same identifier.
